Standardized ratios of a Cox fit

Source: R/standardize_cox.R
standardize.cox.Rd

Indirect or direct standardization of every provider's event count from a Cox model, in the form of the survival measures (SMR, SHR).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cox'
standardize(fit, type = c("indirect", "direct"), providers = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted by fit_cox().

type

"indirect" (default) or "direct".

providers

optional subset of provider identifiers; the baselines always use every fitted row.

...

unused.

Value

A data frame with one row per provider. Indirect: provider, observed, expected, ratio, person_time. Direct: provider, observed (the total \(O\)), expected (\(E^{(j)}\)), ratio, n_pop (the number of fitted rows). Attribute type.

Details

With \(w_i\) the case weights, \(\delta_i\) the event indicator, \((s_i, t_i]\) the at-risk interval and \(\eta_i\) the fitted linear predictor of row \(i\):

  • indirect: \(O_j = \sum_{i \in j} w_i \delta_i\) and \(E_j = \sum_{i \in j} w_i\, e^{\eta_i} [\Lambda_0(t_i) - \Lambda_0(s_i)]\), the events expected for provider \(j\)'s rows at the national baseline \(\Lambda_0\) (the Breslow estimator over every row); ratio \(O_j / E_j\); the expected counts add up to the observed ones;

  • direct: \(E^{(j)} = \sum_i w_i\, e^{\eta_i} [\Lambda_{0j}(t_i) - \Lambda_{0j}(s_i)]\) over every row, the events expected if every patient had provider \(j\)'s own baseline \(\Lambda_{0j}\) (the Breslow estimator over provider \(j\)'s rows at the same coefficients); ratio \(E^{(j)} / O\) with \(O\) the total observed events. Each Breslow increment of provider \(j\) being one weighted event over its risk-set sum \(RS_j(t)\), \(E^{(j)}\) equals \(\sum\) over provider \(j\)'s events of \(w_i\, RS(t_i) / RS_j(t_i)\), the ratio of the population's to the provider's risk-set sums of \(w e^\eta\).

Both baselines are Breslow estimators whatever ties fitted the coefficients. The person-time is \(\sum_{i \in j} (t_i - s_i)\), the grouping variable of the survival measures' empirical null.

References

He K, Schaubel DE (2015). Standardized mortality ratio for evaluating center-specific mortality: assessment and alternative. Statistics in Biosciences, 7, 296-321.

Examples

s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, type = "survival", seed = 1)
ps <- pp_data(s, x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", time = "stop", start = "start",
              event = "event", cutoff = 0, message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_cox(ps)
head(standardize(fit))
#>   provider observed  expected     ratio person_time
#> 1     P001        6  9.113819 0.6583409    17.89913
#> 2     P002       21 24.908704 0.8430788    51.13512
#> 3     P003        8  4.686770 1.7069324    12.64318
#> 4     P004       28 15.174895 1.8451528    35.70869
#> 5     P005       22 15.468878 1.4222104    33.76398
#> 6     P006       21 24.721026 0.8494793    46.92523
head(standardize(fit, type = "direct"))
#>   provider observed expected     ratio n_pop
#> 1     P001      336 199.1986 0.5928530  2679
#> 2     P002      336 288.2112 0.8577714  2679
#> 3     P003      336 531.4106 1.5815790  2679
#> 4     P004      336 596.6812 1.7758369  2679
#> 5     P005      336 475.9018 1.4163744  2679
#> 6     P006      336 277.3695 0.8255045  2679
